title: More clubs and whether societies used bands
summary: He recalls St. Francis Hall and Tishomingo, and says many societies left band use to the family.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, that's how they used to do. But now in the day, it's kind of different. And it's about all the clubs I can think of. Let me see, we had St. Francis Hall. That was Amelia and Willow. St. Francis Hall. And what club did we have back there? They had a club back there. I can't think of the name of that club. What's back there with the head?
Think of it when this thing stops and write it down. Uh-huh.
I told them Tishomingo, Tishomingo, Tishomingo, Randall.
I wonder why they ever got that name. I think that's an Indian name.
I don't know where they got it.

That's a county way up in northeast Mississippi. It's the Tishomingo county. Yeah. And I guess the people in Mississippi got it from the Indian. Did any clubs not use a band when they buried? Any of them have a rule against it?
Well a whole lot of them didn't use bands. And then it wasn't, if the clubs didn't give a band, sometimes it would be up to the family. See sometimes the family don't want no bands.
Oh yeah. I know that. But I mean, say in that constitution.
Well yeah, there was a very, a whole lot of them didn't give a band. Because they just turned out and committed, you know what I mean?
I guess Masons and Oddfellas both use music now.
Well they use it if the family want it, but if they don't want it, they don't use it. They use a committee. See plenty of people don't like no band, they just use a committee.
